findings.reason: as written the node can close on "not attributable" from an empty store that was never the store holding the identity, which destroys the node's whole purpose and would be discovered only after the note landed.
findings.text: §24's done-when licenses the "records cannot identify the process" branch on one fact, "the session-host store holds no record for the window", but that store (`~/.config/reckon/crew/session-hosts/`) is keyed by `pid-start_time` and says nothing about the other sources; measured now, all 91 records have no `updated_at` inside 00:35Z–02:11Z, so the parenthetical is true and yet the identity IS recoverable: the run's own kept record `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261109T013544897285-review-of-a-concurrent-launch-is-refused-34d0376761a9/discard.json` carries `"session": "a337e0e6-c34c-4497-878a-bc42ce1b7cf6"`, and both the follower registration (`…watch/reckon-18dc8a86709b.followers/a337e0e6-…f8728255d227.lock`, `started_at` 2026-11-07T12:13:44Z) and its lease (`renewed_at` 2026-11-09T04:22:44Z, i.e. after the window) are keyed by exactly that session — so the empty session-host store is a true statement standing in for the one the node needs, and the note can take the fallback while a nameable owner sits in the run directory the plan already tells it to read
